findings.title: Report consistency vs. the executor is asserted but not actually guaranteed
findings.problem: The 'no await between reads => consistent snapshot' guarantee holds only if the report builder is strictly synchronous. Reads are not routed through the executor, so if any await separates reading orders from reading coupons, a queued committing checkout can interleave and break the asserted identities (redeemed === count(orders with coupon); generated === available+reserved+redeemed). The spec explicitly requires the report to reconcile, so this interleaving window is a correctness risk.
findings.fix: Make the snapshot rule explicit and enforced: state that reporting.buildReport() must read all needed maps in one synchronous, await-free pass (rule R-REPORT-SYNC), or route the report read through the executor as an ordered read task. Strengthen the Section 14 report test to fire a report call concurrently with a committing checkout via Promise.all and assert the identities still hold.

findings.title: Order-count source of truth is split between successfulOrderCount and count-of-Orders
findings.problem: Milestones use a mutable successfulOrderCount while the report uses count of Orders; nothing states they are the same source, so they can drift and silently break I4 and the generated <= milestonesReached identity.
findings.fix: Define one source of truth: milestoneSequence = orders.size immediately after insertion, and state successfulOrderCount is an alias for orders.size. Removes any counter/collection drift.

findings.title: requestFingerprint omits quantities/line composition yet is presented as the key-reuse integrity guard
findings.problem: The fingerprint covers only cart id and coupon code, not the request-determining quantities/lines. It is presented as the integrity check for 'same key, different params' but covers only two of the inputs that determine the order, leaving 'same request' ambiguous.
findings.fix: Either explicitly document the assumption that makes two fields sufficient (a key maps 1:1 to a cart and a committed cart is immutable) in Sections 7.1 and 17, or include a sorted productId:quantity line signature in the fingerprint.

findings.title: attemptId / reservedBy origin unspecified; reservedBy is write-only
findings.problem: attemptId is never defined ('idempotency key / checkout attempt id' names two different things, and the key is optional). reservedBy is set but never read, since the state machine is enforced by status within one serialized task - a dead field like the removed Product.version.
findings.fix: Either remove reservedBy for the in-memory design (note the multi-instance DB version would use a tx id to scope conditional updates), or define attemptId precisely (e.g. a per-request UUID independent of the optional Idempotency-Key) and state where it is read.

findings.title: Cart/order id generation unspecified; test fixtures assume ids pre-exist
findings.where: Section 10 (POST /carts), Section 4.2 and Section 14 test snippets using cA/cB/c_123
findings.problem: Id generation scheme is never specified, and only products are seeded (not carts). The oversell/concurrency snippets read as if cA/cB/c_123 pre-exist, eliding cart creation and id capture.
findings.fix: Specify id generation (e.g. crypto.randomUUID() for carts/orders) in Section 3/6.1, and adjust the Section 14 snippets to create carts and capture returned ids before firing the two checkouts, keeping determinism anchored to executor FIFO on the checkouts rather than on id values.

findings.title: FIFO 'exactly one 201/one 409' determinism depends on no await before executor.run; state it
findings.problem: The determinism conclusion is stated without its premise: both checkout tasks must enqueue before either body mutates inventory. Adding an await before executor.run in the handler could invert submission order relative to inject order.
findings.fix: Add a rule that the checkout handler calls executor.run(...) with no preceding await, and note tests assert counts (one 201, one 409) and final inventory, not which cart wins.

findings.title: GET /admin/coupons shape omits reservedBy/redeemedByOrderId
findings.problem: The documented list returns status only. Sufficient for the current Section 14 assertions, but flagged for completeness so an implementer does not later find a test needs an omitted field.
findings.fix: Confirm status alone covers all coupon assertions (it does as written), or add reservedBy/redeemedByOrderId to the documented shape if any test asserts reservation ownership. No correctness change required.
